analysis:
The PR change is documentation-only: one added row in the docs/provider/cli-reference.md environment-variable forwarding table (patch hunk near head line 1687) for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES, referencing AdmissionRateEstimators.swift (DeadlineAdmissionFixes.environmentKey). The supplied units (head lines 1-846) do not contain that row, so I verified it only through the patch excerpt. The surrounding text I did examine is existing documentation of the CLI: logout token revocation, cache settings, Autopilot, App Attest worker opt-in and drain behavior. None of it changed in this PR.

The added row introduces no code, no config or auth path, and no change to trust boundaries. It documents an environment variable that is forwarded to the daemon. Whether forwarding it affects security depends on the AdmissionRateEstimators.swift implementation, which is not supplied. The name suggests a scheduling/TTFT deadline-admission tuning knob. That could have availability or TTFT-timing implications (T-041 timing oracle, T-010 DoS, T-029), but no evidence in this batch shows it weakens cache scoping, attestation, encryption or authorization. The forwarding allowlist is an operator-controlled shell value, so it does not give a consumer or remote provider control of the knob. I recorded this as an unverified contract rather than a finding.

No threat-model updates are needed for the documentation row alone. The Swift code that implements and forwards this variable lives in files outside this batch; reviewers of those files should check that the environment passthrough does not bypass safety checks such as admission or memory guards.
